citation: Transcriptome-wide Mendelian randomization study prioritising novel tissue-dependent genes for glioma susceptibility (PMID: 33504897)
sample_size: Glioma GWAS: 7,400 cases and 8,257 controls (GBM 3,112 cases; non-GBM 2,411 cases). eQTL data: brain effective n=1,194; whole blood n=31,684; 13 brain tissues n=114-209.
significance: Reported as robust MR evidence with colocalisation support; specific p-values not given in the abstract.
summary: Integrating multi-tissue eQTLs with glioma GWAS data using Mendelian randomisation and colocalisation, the study found that genetically predicted increased expression of RETREG2 (FAM134A) was associated with glioma risk. RETREG2 was one of three novel glioma susceptibility genes, alongside FAM178B and MVB12B. The effect appeared relatively consistent across glioma subtypes (GBM and non-GBM). This is genetic-association evidence only, with no direct functional experiments on RETREG2.

citation: Bantscheff/Turnbull et al. 2020 - The MiDAC histone deacetylase complex is essential for embryonic development and has a unique multivalent structure (PMID: 32591534)
phenotype: Mice lacking MIDEAS die during late embryogenesis; Phenotype identical to Dnttip1 knockout mice; Heart malformation; Haematopoietic failure; Perturbed gene expression in embryos

citation: Unknown et al. 2025 - A de novo missense variant in MIDEAS results in increased deacetylase activity of the MiDAC HDAC complex causing a neurodevelopmental syndrome (PMID: 41290615)
summary: Two unrelated individuals with a multisystem neurodevelopmental disorder (delayed speech, joint contractures, dysmorphism, gut dysmotility) carry the same de novo heterozygous MIDEAS p.Tyr654Ser variant. CryoEM shows Y654 lies in an auto-inhibitory loop covering the HDAC active site, and the variant is proposed to displace the loop and increase deacetylase activity. Patient fibroblasts show gene expression changes reciprocal to those seen after rapid MiDAC degradation.

citation: Unknown et al. 2020 - The MiDAC histone deacetylase complex is essential for embryonic development and has a unique multivalent structure (PMID: 32591534)
summary: Mice lacking MIDEAS or DNTTIP1 die with identical late-embryonic phenotypes, with heart malformation and haematopoietic failure caused by perturbed gene expression. MiDAC is also needed for chromosome alignment in mitosis in cancer cells. The cryoEM structure shows a unique assembly with four HDAC1 copies at the periphery.

citation: Unknown et al. 2015 - Structural and functional characterization of a cell cycle associated HDAC1/2 complex reveals the structural basis for complex assembly and nucleosome targeting (PMID: 25653165)
summary: MIDEAS is a corepressor in a cell-cycle-associated (mitotic, cyclin A-associated) complex with HDAC1/2 and DNTTIP1. The DNTTIP1 N-terminal dimerization domain interacts with the HDAC1:MIDEAS complex and mediates its assembly, while the C-terminal domain binds DNA and nucleosomes.

citation: Unknown et al. 2020 - The histone deacetylase complex MiDAC regulates a neurodevelopmental gene expression program to control neurite outgrowth (PMID: 32297854)
summary: MiDAC, which contains MIDEAS, regulates a neurodevelopmental gene expression program. It upregulates SLIT3 and NTN1, probably through H4K20ac removal, and represses negative regulators of neurogenesis by reducing H3K27ac. Loss of MiDAC causes neurite outgrowth defects that SLIT3 and/or NTN1 supplementation rescues.

citation: Unknown et al. 2024 - Mitotic deacetylase complex (MiDAC) recognizes the HIV-1 core promoter to control activated viral gene expression (PMID: 38781120)
summary: DNTTIP1 binds the HIV TASHET core promoter element directly and interacts with MIDEAS and HDAC1/2 by co-IP. Gene silencing of MIDEAS, DNTTIP1 and NAT10 showed that MIDEAS is functionally required for Tat-activated HIV expression in cells.

citation: Unknown et al. 2025 - Mutations on the surface of HDAC1 reveal molecular determinants of specific complex assembly and their requirement for gene regulation (PMID: 40966515)
summary: MIDEAS is part of the MiDAC family, one of six HDAC1/2 complex families (SIN3, NuRD, CoREST, MIDAC, MIER, RERE). Comparing MIDEAS:HDAC1 and MTA1:HDAC1 structures identified HDAC1 surface residues needed for binding. HDAC1 Y48E and E63R mutations reduce or abolish binding to MiDAC and other complexes, perturbing gene expression and histone acetylation.

citation: Unknown et al. 2025 - DNA methylation in peripheral blood leukocytes in late onset Alzheimer's disease (PMID: 40343304)
summary: MIDEAS was among the genes differentially methylated in peripheral blood leukocytes of late-onset Alzheimer's disease patients versus controls, in an analysis of public GEO datasets (GSE59685, GSE53740). This is an epigenetic association, not a genetic one.

citation: Corradi et al. 2003 - Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and peripheral neuropathy in Ebf2-null mice (PMID: 12466206)
phenotype: defective migration of GnRH-synthesizing neurons; impaired neuroendocrine axis with secondary hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; impaired pubertal development; peripheral neuropathy with defective axon sorting; hypomyelination; segmental dysmyelination; axonal damage; sharply decreased motor nerve conduction velocity

citation: Chiara et al. 2012 - Motor dysfunction and cerebellar Purkinje cell firing impairment in Ebf2 null mice (PMID: 23000673)
phenotype: locomotor impairment; deficient motor coordination and motor learning; hypotrophic cerebellar cortex with loss of a Purkinje cell subset; altered adult Purkinje cell firing (higher input resistance, increased anomalous rectification, decreased first spike latency, higher initial firing frequency, lower voltage threshold, reduced afterhyperpolarization); normal climbing fiber monoinnervation and normal parallel fiber-Purkinje cell synapse

citation: Chung et al. 2008 - Purkinje cell subtype specification in the cerebellar cortex: early B-cell factor 2 acts to repress the zebrin II-positive Purkinje cell phenotype (PMID: 18403128)
phenotype: selective Purkinje cell death; ectopic expression of zebrin II+ genes in zebrin II- Purkinje cells; cerebellar defects differing in each transverse zone; PLCbeta4 expression and stripe number maintained

citation: Vidal et al. 2011 - Both Schwann cell and axonal defects cause motor peripheral neuropathy in Ebf2-/- mice (PMID: 21220016)
phenotype: delayed onset of myelination; downregulated Schwann cell differentiation markers; isolated clusters of hypomyelinated fibers; nodal abnormalities and shorter internodal length; decreased axonal calibre with lack of large axons; severely impaired motor nerve conduction velocity and amplitude; less affected sensory nerve parameters

citation: Ebf2 and orexin circuit - Aspects of the narcolepsy-cataplexy syndrome in O/E3-null mutant mice (PMID: 21435382)
phenotype: decreased orexin-producing neurons in the lateral hypothalamus; severely impaired orexinergic innervation of the pons; narcoleptic phenotype with direct transitions to REM sleep (DREM); narcolepsy-cataplexy-like sleep-wake abnormalities

citation: Ebf2 and PAG dopamine neurons - Ebf2 is required for development of dopamine neurons in the midbrain periaqueductal gray matter of mouse (PMID: 25762221)
phenotype: marked reduction in the number of dopaminergic neurons in the midbrain periaqueductal gray; substantia nigra and VTA dopamine neurons unaffected

citation: Dynamic Expression and New Functions of Early B Cell Factor 2 in Cerebellar Development (PMID: 31273610)
phenotype: severely hypocellular fastigial cerebellar nuclei; defective development of anterior lobe Purkinje cells

citation: Purkinje cell phenotype restricts the distribution of unipolar brush cells (PMID: 19800947)
phenotype: disrupted Purkinje cell topography due to Purkinje cell death and ectopic gene expression; abnormal topography of unipolar brush cells (homogeneous distribution of CR+ UBCs, increased density of mGluR1alpha+ UBCs, ectopic PLCbeta4+ UBCs); UBC ectopia is non-cell-autonomous

citation: Rajakumari et al. 2013 - EBF2 determines and maintains brown adipocyte identity (PMID: 23499423)
phenotype: loss of brown-specific characteristics in brown adipose cells and tissue; reduced thermogenic capacity

citation: Stine et al. 2016 - EBF2 promotes the recruitment of beige adipocytes in white adipose tissue (PMID: 26844207)
phenotype: failure of subcutaneous WAT and primary adipose cultures to induce UCP1 or a thermogenic program after adrenergic stimulation; impaired beige adipocyte development

citation: Rajakumari et al. 2013 - EBF2 determines and maintains brown adipocyte identity (PMID: 23499423)
summary: EBF2 is a transcription factor selectively expressed in brown relative to white adipocytes. It recruits Pparγ to brown-selective binding sites and reprograms myoblasts and white preadipose cells to a brown fat fate. Ebf2-deficient mice lose brown-specific characteristics and thermogenic capacity.

citation: Shapira et al. 2017 - EBF2 transcriptionally regulates brown adipogenesis via the histone reader DPF3 and the BAF chromatin remodeling complex (PMID: 28428261)
summary: EBF2 binds lineage-specific enhancers in BAT by ChIP-seq. It physically interacts with BRG1 and the BAF complex. Dpf3 is a direct EBF2 target and a brown fat-selective BAF component, and loss of DPF3 reduces chromatin accessibility at EBF2-bound enhancers.

citation: Zhao et al. 2014 - A long noncoding RNA transcriptional regulatory circuit drives thermogenic adipocyte differentiation (PMID: 25002143)
summary: The lncRNA Blnc1 forms a ribonucleoprotein complex with EBF2 to stimulate the thermogenic gene program. Blnc1 is itself an EBF2 target, forming a feedforward loop that drives thermogenic adipogenesis.

citation: Stine et al. 2016 - EBF2 promotes the recruitment of beige adipocytes in white adipose tissue (PMID: 26844207)
summary: Ebf2 knockout mice and primary cultures fail to induce UCP1 or a thermogenic program after adrenergic stimulation. Transgenic EBF2 overexpression in adipose tissue drives beige adipocyte development, even at thermoneutrality. It also increases WAT mitochondrial function and protects against high-fat diet-induced weight gain.

citation: Dynamic Expression and New Functions of Early B Cell Factor 2 in Cerebellar Development (PMID: 31273610)
summary: Genetic fate mapping shows Ebf2 mRNA is initially present in all Purkinje cell progenitors. It is also activated in an early-born subset of anterior-lobe granule cell precursors and is expressed prenatally in projection neurons of all cerebellar nuclei. Ebf2 null mice have severely hypocellular fastigial nuclei.

citation: An ancient role for collier/Olf/Ebf (COE)-type transcription factors in axial motor neuron development (PMID: 30658714)
summary: mEbf2 is expressed in medial motor column spinal motor neurons, and Ebf2 knockout mice show defective differentiation of a subset of these neurons. Transgenic mouse Ebf2 rescues axial motor neuron differentiation and locomotor defects in C. elegans unc-3 mutants, indicating functional conservation.

citation: A genome-wide association study identifies four novel susceptibility loci underlying inguinal hernia (PMID: 26686553)
sample_size: 72,805 discovery subjects (5,295 cases, 67,510 controls); 92,444 replication subjects (9,701 cases, 82,743 controls)
significance: genome-wide significant, replicated in independent cohort
summary: The EBF2 locus is one of four novel inguinal hernia susceptibility loci, alongside EFEMP1, WT1 and ADAMTS6. EBF2 expression was observed in mouse connective tissue.

citation: Deubiquitinating enzyme USP2 regulates brown adipose tissue thermogenesis via controlling EBF2 stabilization (PMID: 40189098)
summary: Proteome-wide analysis identified EBF2 as a substrate of the deubiquitinase USP2. USP2 stabilizes EBF2 and mediates BAT thermogenic function. Usp2 knockdown or inhibition impairs thermogenesis, while Usp2 overexpression protects against diet-induced obesity.

citation: SOX4 facilitates brown fat development and maintenance through EBF2-mediated thermogenic gene program in mice (PMID: 39402212)
summary: SOX4 acts upstream of EBF2 and activates EBF2 transcription, which determines brown fat fate. PKA phosphorylation of SOX4 at S235 promotes its nuclear translocation and EBF2 transcription. SOX4 also cooperates with EBF2 to drive thermogenic gene expression.

citation: Elevated EBF2 in mouse but not pig drives the progressive brown fat lineage specification via chromatin activation (PMID: 39736442)
summary: EBF2 interacts with CBP/P300 to deposit H3K27ac and activate chromatin at BAT-associated genes, driving brown fat specification and diverting cells from the muscle lineage. Both mouse and pig EBF2 stimulate adipogenesis in multipotent mesodermal stem cells. Pig EBF2 expression is depleted during the critical specification window, which explains the absence of porcine BAT.

citation: Sapap4 deficiency leads to postsynaptic defects and abnormal behaviors relevant to hyperkinetic neuropsychiatric disorder in mice (PMID: 35368073)
phenotype: reduced spine density in the prefrontal cortex; abnormal PSD composition: reduced PSD95, GluR1 and GluR2, increased SHANK3; hyperactivity; impulsivity; reduced despair/depression-like behavior; hypersensitivity to low-dose amphetamine; memory deficits; decreased prepulse inhibition; mania-like phenotype; hyperactivity partially rescued by valproate

citation: Cognitive impairment and autistic-like behaviour in SAPAP4-deficient mice (PMID: 30664629)
phenotype: cognitive deficits; impaired vocal communication; impaired social interaction; autism-like behaviors; altered synapse morphology, function and plasticity

citation: Novel role of the synaptic scaffold protein Dlgap4 in ventricular surface integrity and neuronal migration during cortical development (PMID: 35585091)
phenotype: in utero electroporation of Dlgap4 knockdown caused a ventricular surface phenotype; altered progenitor cell dynamics, morphology and proliferation; neuronal migration defects; disorganized radial glial adherens junction components; altered actin cytoskeleton dynamics at the apical domain; phenotype rescued by wild-type but not mutant DLGAP4; Dlgap4 heterozygous knockout mice show developmental defects in the dorsal telencephalon

citation: Novel role of the synaptic scaffold protein Dlgap4 in ventricular surface integrity and neuronal migration during cortical development (PMID: 35585091)
sample_size: 1 patient; mouse in utero electroporation and heterozygous KO cohorts
summary: DLGAP4 is strongly expressed in the mouse ventricular zone from early corticogenesis and interacts with key VZ proteins including EML1. A novel DLGAP4 variant was found in a patient with an EML1-like subcortical heterotopia phenotype. Dlgap4 knockdown disrupted radial glial adherens junctions, actin dynamics and neuronal migration, and was rescued by wild-type but not mutant DLGAP4. Heterozygous KO mice show dorsal telencephalon defects.

citation: Cognitive impairment and autistic-like behaviour in SAPAP4-deficient mice (PMID: 30664629)
summary: SAPAP4 (DLGAP4)-deficient mice show cognitive deficits, impaired vocal communication and impaired social interaction, resembling ASD. They also show altered synapse morphology, function and plasticity. This indicates DLGAP4 is critical for functional neuronal network development.

citation: Epigenetic remodelling and dysregulation of DLGAP4 is linked with early-onset cerebellar ataxia (PMID: 24986922)
summary: The t(8;20)(p12;q11.23) translocation truncates DLGAP4 and co-segregates with cerebellar ataxia in a five-generation family. It causes monoallelic hypermethylation of the DLGAP4 promoter CpG island and chromatin remodelling. This results in dysregulated, monoallelic expression of DLGAP4 mRNAs and ncRNAs in carriers.

citation: ASHG 2010 - A familial translocation as a model for decoding regulatory mechanisms associated with an inherited epimutation
summary: The long brain-specific DLGAP4 isoform is specifically expressed in fetal and adult cerebellum, particularly the Purkinje cell layer in both mouse and human. The widely expressed short isoform shows elevated monoallelic expression from the translocated allele. The translocation makes DLGAP4 a candidate gene for early-onset non-progressive cerebellar ataxia.

citation: Bipolar Disorder Associated microRNA, miR-1908-5p, Regulates the Expression of Genes Functioning in Neuronal Glutamatergic Synapses (PMID: 28035180)
summary: DLGAP4 was identified and validated as a target of the bipolar disorder-associated miR-1908-5p, together with GRIN1, STX1A, CLSTN1 and GRM4, all of which function in glutamatergic synapses. In human brain expression profiles, miR-1908-5p and its synaptic targets are inversely correlated.

citation: Circular RNA DLGAP4 Ameliorates Ischemic Stroke Outcomes by Targeting miR-143 to Regulate Endothelial-Mesenchymal Transition Associated with Blood-Brain Barrier Integrity (PMID: 29114076)
sample_size: 26 stroke patients (13 female, 13 male); mouse tMCAO model
summary: circDLGAP4 acts as a miR-143 sponge, which relieves repression of HECTD1. Its levels are decreased in plasma of ischemic stroke patients and in a mouse stroke model. Overexpression reduced infarct size, neurological deficits and blood-brain barrier damage, and inhibited endothelial-mesenchymal transition in the tMCAO mouse model.

citation: Circular RNA DLGAP4 alleviates sevoflurane-induced neurotoxicity by regulating miR-9-5p/Sirt1/BDNF pathway (PMID: 38000773)
summary: circDLGAP4 expression falls with sevoflurane exposure in neonatal mouse hippocampus and HT22 cells. Overexpression increased viability and reduced apoptosis and TNF-α/IL-6. It acts by directly sponging miR-9-5p and so upregulating Sirt1/BDNF.

citation: Circular RNA DLGAP4 is down-regulated and negatively correlates with severity, inflammatory cytokine expression and pro-inflammatory gene miR-143 expression in acute ischemic stroke patients (PMID: 31933904)
summary: PBMC circ-DLGAP4 is down-regulated in AIS patients (AUC 0.816). It correlates negatively with NIHSS score, CRP, inflammatory cytokines and miR-143.

citation: DLGAP4 acts as an effective prognostic predictor for hepatocellular carcinoma and is closely related to tumour progression (PMID: 36396671)
sample_size: TCGA HCC cohort; HCC cell lines and xenografts
significance: independent risk factor in multivariate Cox analysis
summary: DLGAP4 is overexpressed in HCC tissues and cell lines, and high expression is an independent poor-prognosis factor. Knockdown inhibited HCC proliferation and metastasis in vitro and in vivo and lowered PPARβ/δ protein. Overexpression had the opposite effects.

citation: Examination of the expression and prognostic significance of DLGAPs in gastric cancer using the TCGA database and bioinformatic analysis (PMID: 30365066)
significance: significant association with overall survival reported
summary: DLGAP4 is selectively upregulated in gastric cancer tissues compared with normal tissue, and high expression correlates with shorter overall survival. This was confirmed at mRNA and protein level by RT-qPCR and IHC, suggesting an oncogenic role.

citation: Murakami et al. 2015 - CTRP6 is an endogenous complement regulator that can effectively treat induced arthritis (PMID: 26404464)
phenotype: C1qtnf6-/- mice highly susceptible to induced arthritis due to enhanced complement activation; C1qtnf6-transgenic mice refractory to arthritis; Enhanced Arthus reaction in knockout mice; Enhanced experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis in knockout mice; Knockout embryos semi-lethal; CTRP6 suppresses the alternative complement pathway by competing with factor B for C3(H2O) binding; Intra-articular recombinant human CTRP6 cured arthritis in arthritis-induced mice

citation: CTRP6 rapidly responds to acute nutritional changes, regulating adipose tissue expansion and inflammation in mice (PMID: 34632797)
phenotype: CTRP6-KO MEFs showed increased adipogenic gene expression (Pparg, Fabp4, Adipoq); CTRP6-KO MEFs showed markedly reduced inflammatory genes (Tnf-α, Ccl2, Il6); 3-day high-fat feeding of CTRP6-KO mice induced greater whole body and adipose tissue weight gain than wild-type littermates

citation: Sun et al. 2015 - CTRP6 is an endogenous complement regulator that can effectively treat induced arthritis (PMID: 26404464)
summary: CTRP6 (C1qtnf6) specifically suppresses the alternative complement pathway by competing with factor B for C3(H2O) binding. C1qtnf6-/- mice are highly susceptible to induced arthritis, have enhanced Arthus reaction and EAE, and their embryos are semi-lethal. C1qtnf6-transgenic mice are refractory to arthritis, and recombinant human CTRP6 cures arthritis. CTRP6 is expressed in human synoviocytes and elevated in RA patients.

citation: C1QTNF6 participates in the pathogenesis of PCOS by affecting the inflammatory response of granulosa cells (PMID: 33959757)
summary: C1QTNF6 is elevated in serum and granulosa cells of PCOS patients and in PCOS mouse serum and ovary. Its overexpression raises CRP, IL6 and TNFα and activates AKT/NF-κB signaling in LPS-treated KGN cells. Knockdown or an NF-κB inhibitor reverses these effects.

citation: MiR-29b-3p promotes particulate matter-induced inflammatory responses by regulating the C1QTNF6/AMPK pathway (PMID: 31955152)
summary: miR-29b-3p directly targets C1QTNF6 (RNA-seq and luciferase reporter) in human bronchial epithelial cells. C1QTNF6 protects against PM-induced inflammation by activating AMPK signaling. In mice, miR-29b-3p antagomirs blocked PM-induced C1QTNF6 downregulation in lung and reduced inflammation.

citation: Long non-coding RNA H19 promotes leukocyte inflammation in ischemic stroke by targeting the miR-29b/C1QTNF6 axis (PMID: 35322553)
summary: C1QTNF6 is upregulated in leukocytes of stroke patients and MCAO rats. miR-29b binds C1QTNF6 mRNA and represses it, while lncRNA H19 sponges miR-29b to maintain C1QTNF6 expression. C1QTNF6 overexpression increased IL-1β and TNF-α release and worsened blood-brain barrier disruption and ischemic injury.

citation: C1QTNF6 regulates cell proliferation and apoptosis of NSCLC in vitro and in vivo (PMID: 33269376)
summary: C1QTNF6 promoted proliferation, migration and invasion and reduced apoptosis in SPCA1 and A549 NSCLC cells. C1QTNF6 downregulation weakened xenograft tumor growth in vivo.

citation: C1QTNF6 promotes oral squamous cell carcinoma by enhancing proliferation and inhibiting apoptosis (PMID: 34906149)
summary: C1QTNF6 is overexpressed in OSCC tissue (IHC and TCGA). Knockdown in CaL27 and SCC-9 cells reduced proliferation, caused G2/M arrest, increased apoptosis and inhibited xenograft growth. Microarray and IPA showed activation of Acute Phase Response signaling after silencing.

citation: C1QTNF6 is a Prognostic Biomarker and Related to Immune Infiltration and Drug Sensitivity: A Pan-Cancer Analysis (PMID: 35401204)
summary: C1QTNF6 is overexpressed across many cancer types (TCGA/GTEx) and independently predicts poor survival. Its expression correlates positively with hallmark pathway scores, tumor microenvironment pathways and immune infiltration. Higher expression predicts resistance to most of 198 drugs.

citation: C1QTNF6 as a Novel Diagnostic and Prognostic Biomarker for Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma (PMID: 32282241)
summary: C1QTNF6 is overexpressed in ccRCC and correlates with clinical progression. It is a diagnostic biomarker (ROC) and an independent risk factor for overall survival. GSEA links it to cell cycle, EMT and angiogenesis pathways.

citation: C1QTNF6 Targeted by MiR-184 Regulates the Proliferation, Migration, and Invasion of Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells (PMID: 35578071)
summary: miR-184 binds the C1QTNF6 3'UTR (dual-luciferase) and downregulates its expression in LUAD cells. High C1QTNF6 promotes LUAD cell proliferation, migration and invasion, and miR-184 restrains these processes via C1QTNF6.

citation: Localization and expression of C1QTNF6 in chicken follicles and its regulatory effect on follicular granulosa cells (PMID: 39566174)
summary: Chicken C1QTNF6 is widely expressed in follicle tissues, predominantly in granulosa cells (qRT-PCR and FISH), and is induced by FSH and LH. Overexpression and knockdown affect granulosa cell proliferation and apoptosis, and C1QTNF6 reduces steroidogenic gene expression and progesterone and estrogen output. It also inhibits AdipoR1 expression.

citation: Mice null for NEDD9 (HEF1α) display extensive hippocampal dendritic spine loss and cognitive impairment (PMID: 26683084)
phenotype: Deficits in learning and memory recall in the Morris water maze; Extensive loss of dendritic spine density in the dentate gyrus and CA1; Spine loss across all branch orders and dendrite regions; Age-dependent spine loss (1.5, 6 and 10 months); No change in gross hippocampal morphology; No evidence of altered neurogenesis (BrdU stereology)

citation: The scaffold protein NEDD9 is necessary for leukemia-cell migration and disease progression in a mouse model of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (PMID: 35523865)
phenotype: Delayed CLL development; Markedly reduced disease burden; Significant survival benefit; Impaired CLL cell homing, chemotaxis, migration and adhesion

citation: Nedd9 Restrains Autophagy to Limit Growth of Early Stage Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (PMID: 34006524)
phenotype: Larger tumors with accelerated growth and elevated proliferation in KPN versus KP mice; Cell-autonomous effect shown by orthotopic transplantation; Reduced SRC and AKT activation; Increased active LKB1/AMPK and increased autophagy; Growth advantage eliminated by chloroquine
knockout_type: full knockout (Nedd9 deletion in the KP lung cancer model)

citation: A requirement for Nedd9 in luminal progenitor cells prior to mammary tumorigenesis in MMTV-HER2/ErbB2 mice (PMID: 23318423)
phenotype: Tumor incidence reduced to 18% versus 80% in wild-type; Increased tumor latency; Limited effect on metastasis; Reduced number and colony-forming potential of luminal mammary progenitors; Mammosphere morphology and polarity defects; Decreased FAK expression and increased sensitivity to FAK and SRC inhibitors

citation: Nedd9 restrains renal cystogenesis in Pkd1-/- mice (PMID: 25139996)
phenotype: Nedd9 ablation alone did not influence cystogenesis; Strongly enhanced cyst formation in Pkd1-/-;Nedd9-/- mice; Ciliary morphological defects and loss of ciliary adenylate cyclase III; Ciliary resorption defects; Enhanced Src, Erk and S6 activation; Reduced Ca2+ response to stimuli
knockout_type: full knockout (combined with inducible Pkd1 knockout)

citation: Identification of Nedd9 as a TGF-β-Smad2/3 Target Gene Involved in RANKL-Induced Osteoclastogenesis by Comprehensive Analysis (PMID: 27336669)
phenotype: Reduced RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis in Nedd9-deficient cells; Partially abrogated stimulatory effect of TGF-β on osteoclastogenesis; No abnormal skeletal phenotype in knockout mice

citation: NEDD9 stabilizes focal adhesions, increases binding to the extra-cellular matrix and differentially effects 2D versus 3D cell migration (PMID: 22509381)
phenotype: Increased focal adhesion disassembly rate with increased paxillin phosphorylation; Increased 2D migration but reduced 3D collagen migration; Decreased adhesion to fibronectin; Suppressed β1 integrin activation; Altered myosin light chain kinase activation
knockout_type: full knockout (MEFs derived from Nedd9-/- mice)

citation: NEDD9 depletion destabilizes Aurora A kinase and heightens the efficacy of Aurora A inhibitors: implications for treatment of metastatic solid tumors (PMID: 23539442)
phenotype: Decreased AURKA with increased ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation upon NEDD9 loss; Increased sensitivity to AURKA inhibitors; Combined NEDD9 shRNA and AURKA inhibitor impaired tumor growth and distant metastasis in breast xenografts
knockout_type: knockdown (shRNA in xenografts) and knockout cells

citation: NEDD9 promotes lung cancer metastasis through epithelial-mesenchymal transition (PMID: 24174333)
phenotype: NEDD9 knockdown inhibited migration, invasion and metastasis of lung cancer cells in vitro and in vivo; Reduced EMT and FAK activation
knockout_type: knockdown (in xenograft) and Nedd9 mouse spontaneous metastasis models

citation: Susceptibility-Associated Genetic Variation in NEDD9 Contributes to Prostate Cancer Initiation and Progression (PMID: 33632899)
phenotype: NEDD9 promoted prostate cancer tumor growth and metastasis in vivo

citation: Unknown et al. 2025 - EIF4A3 Promotes Muscle Atrophy and Aging by Inhibiting the FAK Pathway Through NEDD9 mRNA Destabilization (PMID: 40641186)
sample_size: n=5 human young/aged; n=6-10 mice per group
summary: NEDD9 mRNA is a direct target of the EJC helicase EIF4A3, which promotes its decay. Loss of NEDD9 reduces FAK and PI3K-Akt signaling and promotes muscle atrophy and aging in myotubes and mice. Pharmacological activation of the NEDD9-FAK pathway abolished the pro-atrophy effects of EIF4A3.

citation: Nedd9 restrains renal cystogenesis in Pkd1-/- mice (PMID: 25139996)
summary: Nedd9 expression is deregulated in human ADPKD and a mouse model. Nedd9 loss in Pkd1-/- mice exacerbates cystogenesis, causes ciliary defects and resorption failure through impaired Aurora-A activation, and enhances Src, Erk and S6 signaling. Nedd9 therefore acts as a modifier of ADPKD.

citation: Retinoic acid regulates Schwann cell migration via NEDD9 induction by transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms (PMID: 27085739)
summary: Retinoic acid upregulates NEDD9 in Schwann cells through increased mRNA levels and increased protein stability, and it alters the NEDD9 phospho-isoform ratio. NEDD9 silencing did not affect basal migration but abolished RA-enhanced migration.

citation: NEDD9 links anaplastic thyroid cancer stemness to chromosomal instability through integrated centrosome asymmetry and DNA sensing regulation (PMID: 35449243)
summary: NEDD9 is transcriptionally upregulated and co-expressed with ALDH1A3 in ALDH+ stem-like anaplastic thyroid cancer cells. NEDD9 silencing abolished tolerance of centrosome amplification and micronuclei, including the suppression of STING. It also reduced stemness, CIN and tumor growth in vitro and in vivo, and enhanced paclitaxel effectiveness.

citation: SOX2 promotes hypoxia-induced breast cancer cell migration by inducing NEDD9 expression and subsequent activation of Rac1/HIF-1α signaling (PMID: 31462898)
summary: Hypoxia increases NEDD9 mRNA and protein in breast cancer cells. SOX2 is a positive transcriptional regulator of NEDD9, shown by promoter-luciferase assays and SOX2 knockdown. NEDD9 silencing attenuated hypoxia-induced Rac1 activity and HIF-1α expression, and with them cell migration.

citation: Overexpression of NEDD9 is associated with altered expression of E-Cadherin, β-Catenin and N-Cadherin and predictive of poor prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 23086683)
summary: NEDD9 was overexpressed in 56.2% of NSCLC samples by IHC relative to normal lung. Overexpression correlated with altered E-cadherin, β-catenin and N-cadherin (EMT markers), lymph node metastasis and shorter overall survival. It was an independent prognostic factor.

citation: NEDD9 sustains hexokinase expression to promote glycolysis (PMID: 35410460)
summary: NEDD9 knockdown impaired glycolysis in lung cancer cells and post-transcriptionally reduced HK1, HK2, PFK1 and GAPDH. These enzymes were also reduced in KP mouse lung tumors with null Nedd9. Hexokinase depletion or 2DG raised NEDD9 expression, suggesting a negative feedback loop.

citation: Baicalein inhibits pancreatic cancer cell proliferation and invasion via suppression of NEDD9 expression and its downstream Akt and ERK signaling pathways (PMID: 28915595)
summary: Baicalein suppressed NEDD9 expression in pancreatic cancer cells, lowering Akt and ERK activity. Akt T308 phosphorylation fell through reduced NEDD9-dependent PDK1 expression. NEDD9 overexpression rescued proliferation and invasion.

citation: SPAG9 regulates HEF1 expression and drives EMT in bladder transitional cell carcinoma via rac1 signaling pathway (PMID: 30662804)
summary: SPAG9 regulates HEF1/NEDD9 expression in bladder cancer cells. SPAG9 overexpression increased migration through HEF1 upregulation and activated Rac1, whereas SPAG9 silencing reduced HEF1 and Rac1 activity. SPAG9 also affected EMT markers (E-cadherin, vimentin).

citation: Glucocorticoid Receptors Drive Breast Cancer Cell Migration and Metabolic Reprogramming via PDK4 (PMID: 37224504)
summary: NEDD9 was identified as a dexamethasone- and pSer134-GR-dependent regulated gene in TNBC cells. It is part of a gene set controlling cell migration alongside CSF1 and RUNX3.

citation: Aicardi Syndrome Is a Genetically Heterogeneous Disorder (PMID: 37628618)
variant_detail: Unique de novo variant in KMT2B (specific notation not given in abstract)
phenotype: Aicardi syndrome or suspected Aicardi syndrome (female); Agenesis of corpus callosum / chorioretinal lacunae / infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (classical triad; patient-specific features not given in abstract)
diagnostic_reason: De novo variant identified by exome/genome sequencing in a female with AIC or suspected AIC; one of five candidate autosomal genes identified.

citation: A New Pathologic KMT2B Variant Associated with Childhood Onset Dystonia Presenting as Variable Phenotypes among Family Members (PMID: 35415007)

citation: KMT2A and KMT2B Mediate Memory Function by Affecting Distinct Genomic Regions (PMID: 28723559)

citation: Tsga8 is required for spermatid morphogenesis and male fertility in mice (PMID: 33766931)

citation: KMT2B promotes the growth of renal cell carcinoma via upregulation of SNHG12 expression and promotion of CEP55 transcription (PMID: 35597996)

citation: Genetic landscape of non-UV-induced cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas (PMID: 41132030)

citation: Adult-onset KMT2B-related dystonia (PMID: 36483457)

citation: Regulation of cortical neurogenesis by MED13L via transcriptional priming and its implications for MED13L syndrome (PMID: 40775066)
summary: Med13l knockout mice are neonatal lethal with reduced brain volume and cortical thickness. Heterozygotes are viable and show learning/memory deficits, reduced motor coordination, anxiety and microcephaly. Single-cell transcriptomics showed impaired neural progenitor differentiation. MED13L primes transcriptional activation of Neurod2, Sox5, Auts2 and Nfib by binding the core Mediator and facilitating its association with RNA Pol II.

citation: Expression Analyses of Mediator Complex Subunit 13-Like: A Responsible Gene for Neurodevelopmental Disorders during Mouse Brain Development (PMID: 33794529)
summary: MED13L expression is tissue- and developmental stage-dependent in mouse. It is enriched in the ventricular zone and in cytoplasm and nucleus of cortical plate neurons at E14, and becomes diffusely cytoplasmic by P30. It partially colocalizes with synaptophysin and PSD95 in cultured hippocampal neurons, suggesting a role in CNS development and synaptic function.

citation: ASHG 2022 - MED13L knockout in cerebral organoids leads to a shifted developmental program through abnormal cis-regulatory element activation
summary: In MED13L knockout hiPSC-derived cerebral organoids, scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq showed only neuroretinal cells, whereas wild-type organoids produced cortical neurons. Neuroretinal OTX2 and PAX6 cis-regulatory elements were aberrantly activated and forebrain OTX2 CREs (AN1, AN2) were not. Neuroretinal genes such as CRX, VSX and USH2A were upregulated, indicating MED13L is needed for proper enhancer activation during neural induction.

citation: Molecular and Functional Characterisation of a Novel Intragenic 12q24.21 Deletion Resulting in MED13L Haploinsufficiency Syndrome (PMID: 37512036)
summary: CRISPR-Cas9 editing of MED13L in control skin fibroblasts reduced cell viability, accelerated aging, and inhibited expression of RB1, E2F1 and CCNC. The patient's exon 3-10 deletion is predicted to produce a truncated protein lacking the MedPIWI and Med13_C domains.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Functional analysis of MED13L missense variants
summary: MED13L is a CDK8-kinase module subunit of Mediator, paralogous to MED13. Seven de novo missense variants cluster in exons 15-17 and 25-31, predicted to disrupt phosphorylation and ubiquitination sites respectively. FBXW7-dependent ubiquitination assays, phosphorylation assays, localization analysis and zebrafish RNA rescue assays were used to test their consequences.

citation: ASHG 2012 - De novo translocation disrupting Mediator complex subunit in a patient with Pierre-Robin sequence and developmental delay

citation: Interactions Between Dietary Metabolites and Regulatory Risk Variants for Human Colon Cancer (PMID: 40964363)

citation: Integrative functional genomics and fine-mapping identify regulatory mechanisms of multivariate obesity GWAS and its cardiometabolic implications (PMID: 41570977)

citation: ASHG 2014 - A Novel Mutation, p.(Lys1474*), in a Female adds Seizures and Ptosis to Clinical Findings in MED13L Haploinsufficiency Syndrome
summary: MED13L is a Mediator subunit acting as a transcriptional coactivator for most RNA Pol II genes, and is highly expressed in early heart and brain development. Gene dosage matters: loss-of-function causes haploinsufficiency syndrome, while a 12q24.2 triplication gives a milder phenotype.

citation: MED13L haploinsufficiency syndrome: A de novo frameshift and recurrent intragenic deletions due to parental mosaicism (PMID: 28371282)

citation: Distinct fetal Ank-1 and Ank-2 related proteins and mRNAs in normal and nb/nb mice (PMID: 8471772)

citation: Two novel ANK1 loss-of-function mutations in Chinese families with hereditary spherocytosis (PMID: 31016877)

citation: Macrocephaly and developmental delay caused by missense variants in RAB5C (PMID: 37552066)
summary: 12 individuals carried 9 de novo heterozygous RAB5C variants. citation: RAB5C Increases Endothelial Release of VWF by Regulating Vesicle Trafficking (PMID: 41537263)
summary: RAB5C was nominated by GWAS for VWF levels. Two VWF-associated variants (rs9915255, rs9912088) regulate RAB5C expression in stem cell-derived endothelial cells. RAB5C silencing reduced histamine-stimulated VWF release, while overexpression of wild-type or constitutively active RAB5C increased it. Proximity labeling found 147 proximal proteins, and SNAP29 was identified as a key interactor mediating VWF exocytosis.

citation: Rab5c-mediated endocytic trafficking regulates hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell development via Notch and AKT signaling (PMID: 32275659)
summary: In zebrafish, Rab5c deficiency impairs HSPC production. Rab5c drives endocytic trafficking of Notch ligands and receptor for hemogenic endothelium specification. citation: S100P is a ferroptosis suppressor to facilitate hepatocellular carcinoma development by rewiring lipid metabolism (PMID: 39779666)

citation: Novel Host Protein TBC1D16, a GTPase Activating Protein of Rab5C, Inhibits Prototype Foamy Virus Replication (PMID: 34367131)
summary: TBC1D16 is a Rab GAP that targets Rab5C and suppresses PFV replication. TBC1D16 is downregulated after PFV infection. Its TBC-domain residues R494 and Q531 are essential for the antiviral effect, and it enhances PFV-induced IFN-β.

citation: RAB5c orchestrates LC3-associated phagocytosis to promote microbicidal function of macrophages (PMID: 42102192)
summary: RAB5c is the RAB5 isoform required for LC3-associated phagocytosis. It regulates phagosome recruitment of the PI(3)P and ROS-generating complexes and promotes V-ATPase translocation, which is needed for ATG16L1 binding and LC3 conjugation. citation: Rab5 isoforms orchestrate a "division of labor" in the endocytic network; Rab5C modulates Rac-mediated cell motility (PMID: 24587345)

citation: Rab5C enhances resistance to ionizing radiation in rectal cancer (PMID: 30968159)

summary: Proteomics of rectal adenocarcinoma biopsies found Rab5C, Ku70 and Ku80 increased after chemoradiation. A radioresistant cell line also overexpressed them. Rab5C modulates EGFR internalization and nuclear relocalization, which affects Ku70/Ku80 expression and radioresistance.

citation: RAB5C, a new mRNA binding target of HuR, regulates breast cancer cell proliferation (PMID: 36480789)
summary: RAB5C is upregulated in breast cancer tissues and in MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 cells. HuR binds the RAB5C 3'UTR and stabilizes its mRNA, and HuR knockdown lowers RAB5C. RAB5C suppression reduces breast cancer cell growth, consistent with an oncogenic role.

citation: The small GTPase Rab5c is a key regulator of trafficking of the CD93/Multimerin-2/β1 integrin complex in endothelial cell adhesion and migration (PMID: 31138217)
summary: In HUVECs and HDBECs, Rab5c silencing showed it drives CD93 recycling to the cell surface. In the Rab5c endosomal compartment, CD93 forms a complex with Multimerin-2 and active β1 integrin, which is recycled by clathrin-independent endocytosis during EC adhesion and migration.

citation: Ait-Lounis et al. 2010 - The transcription factor Rfx3 regulates beta-cell differentiation, function, and glucokinase expression (PMID: 20413507)

citation: Baas et al. 2006 - A deficiency in RFX3 causes hydrocephalus associated with abnormal differentiation of ependymal cells (PMID: 16930429)
summary: Rfx3-deficient mice develop hydrocephalus. RFX3 is strongly expressed in ependymal cells of the subcommissural organ, choroid plexus and ventricular walls. citation: Chen et al. 2018 - Auto-fatty acylation of transcription factor RFX3 regulates ciliogenesis (PMID: 30127002)
summary: RFX3 undergoes enzyme-independent auto S-fatty acylation at a conserved cysteine in its dimerization domain, preferring stearic and oleic acid. citation: Didon et al. 2013 - RFX3 modulation of FOXJ1 regulation of cilia genes in the human airway epithelium (PMID: 23822649)

RFX3 alone did not induce cilia genes, but combined with FOXJ1 it enhanced ciliated gene promoter activity and mRNA expression beyond FOXJ1 alone, which makes RFX3 a co-activator of FOXJ1 in ciliated cell differentiation.

citation: 2002 - Role for RFX transcription factors in non-neuronal cell-specific inactivation of the microtubule-associated protein MAP1A promoter (PMID: 12411430)
summary: RFX1 and RFX3 bind RFX sites in exon 1 of the MAP1A 5' promoter in vitro. RFX3, which is abundant in neuronal cells, down-regulated MAP1A promoter activity when expressed in non-neuronal cells but not in neuronal cells.

citation: 2019 - Evidence that 6q25.1 variant rs6931104 confers susceptibility to chronic myeloid leukemia through RMND1 regulation (PMID: 31237926)
summary: The CML-associated 6q25.1 SNP rs6931104 acts as an eQTL for RMND1. In ChIP assays the A allele changed RFX3 binding affinity compared with the G allele. RFX3 binding affects RMND1 expression in BCR-ABL1+ cell lines.

citation: 2022 - CircRFX3 Up-regulates Its Host Gene RFX3 to Facilitate Tumorigenesis and Progression of Glioma (PMID: 35416616)
summary: CircRFX3 recruits HNRNPK to stabilize RFX3 mRNA in glioma cells. RFX3 in turn promotes PROX1 transcription, which drives glioma cell malignant behavior and tumor growth.

citation: Multi-generational mitochondrial complex V deficiency due to the recurrent ATP5F1A c.620G>A (p.Arg207His) pathogenic variant: A novel family and a review of the literature (PMID: 42520343)

citation: Overexpression of ATP5F1A in Cardiomyocytes Promotes Cardiac Reverse Remodeling (PMID: 38910562)

summary: Single-nucleus RNA-seq showed ATP5F1A was higher in cardiomyocytes from patients with cardiac reverse remodeling (CRR) after LVAD than in the other groups. citation: Lactylation of Mitochondrial ATP Synthase Subunit Alpha Regulates Vascular Remodeling and Progression of Aortic Dissection (PMID: 40800583)

citation: Mourier et al. 2015 - Mitofusin 2 is required to maintain mitochondrial coenzyme Q levels (PMID: 25688136)

citation: Chen et al. 2007 - Mitochondrial fusion protects against neurodegeneration in the cerebellum (PMID: 17693261)

citation: Mitochondria-ER contact mediated by MFN2-SERCA2 interaction supports CD8+ T cell metabolic fitness and function in tumors (PMID: 37738362)

Mfn2 deletion in CD8+ T cells impairs metabolism and promotes tumor growth. MFN2 expression correlates positively with prognosis across multiple cancers.

citation: Mfn2 Regulates High Glucose-Induced MAMs Dysfunction and Apoptosis in Podocytes via PERK Pathway (PMID: 34988075)

Mfn2 knockdown causes MAM loss, mitochondrial dysfunction, PERK activation and apoptosis, while Mfn2 overexpression reverses these effects.

citation: MFN2 coordinates mitochondria motility with α-tubulin acetylation and this regulation is disrupted in CMT2A (PMID: 38883841)

citation: Regulatory roles of external cholesterol in human airway epithelial mitochondrial function through STARD3 signalling (PMID: 35678098)

citation: Cohesin complex-associated holoprosencephaly (PMID: 31334757)

citation: Genetic determinants of micronucleus formation in vivo (PMID: 38355793)

citation: Sororin actively maintains sister chromatid cohesion (PMID: 26903600)
